transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I'm Ruth. Well, what really scared me enough to come in today is... it's something happening at work. I work in a surveillance room, and lately, during the quiet stretches, I keep hearing these voices coming through the monitor speakers. They say things to me like, you missed it, Ruth, or they tell me people are going to get hurt because of me. 

But the thing is, every single channel is muted. No one else hears anything at all. It just really frightened me, so... that is why I decided I needed to be seen.
How long have you been experiencing these voices?
It has been going on for about four months now. It started right around the time I was moved into the lead casino surveillance role.
During these past four months, have you experienced any periods where your mood felt unusually elevated, or conversely, significantly lower than your typical baseline?

I haven't had any periods where I felt elevated or unusually happy, no. But lower... yes, definitely. 

Most days, I feel like this heavy, gray mood just settles over me before I even manage to get out of bed in the morning. It's... it's just really hard to shake. And it gets to the point where I can be sitting in my car before my shift starts, and I'll just start tearing up over nothing more than seeing the casino lights. So, my mood has definitely been a lot lower than my normal baseline.
Have these periods of low mood been present during times when you were not hearing the voices?

No, they really seem to be tied together. Before this whole stretch of feeling so hopeless and guilty after the surveillance lead change, I had never heard any accusations coming through the equipment. And I never felt so certain that I was dangerous to everyone, either. The voices, and those beliefs... they only seem to be part of this same low period.

Looking back at your life, have you ever experienced a period like this before—where you felt this low and hopeless for several months at a time—or is this the very first time you have ever felt this way?

No, this is... this is the first time. I've never had anything like this happen before. I mean, I've had bad days, sure, but never months of feeling this heavy and hopeless. This is all completely new to me.
When you hear these voices or have these thoughts about being dangerous, do you also feel like you are being watched or monitored by the people around you in a way that feels threatening?

No, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, I don't feel like the people around me are watching me or trying to threaten me. It's... it's really just the voices coming through the equipment, and that heavy feeling I have about being a danger. But as far as people actually monitoring me in real life, no, I haven't noticed anything like that.
